item.title: Israel president welcomes Boy George, rare supportive pop star
item.description:
All eyes are on Israel's president as he is expected this week to name the person tasked with forming the next government. But first, on Monday, he had another important guest -- Boy George.

The British singer, a rare Western pop celebrity who not only defies pro-Palestinian calls to boycott Israel but is an outspoken supporter of the country, is visiting for two concerts in Tel Aviv.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis advance to within 80 km of Aden, sources say
item.description:
By Mohammed Ghobari

Nov 2 (Reuters) - Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis have advanced to within 80 km (50 miles) of Aden, the main stronghold and temporary capital of the country's internationally recognised government, four military sources told Reuters on Monday.

The advance brings theHouthis closer to Aden than at any point since the early months of the war in 2015, when they briefly entered the city before being driven out.

item.title: Displaced Palestinians return to damaged Hebron quarter as Israeli troops withdraw
item.description:
HEBRON, West Bank, Nov 2 (Reuters) - Palestinians returned to damaged homes in Hebron in the occupied West Bank on Monday after the Israeli military concluded a 10-day operation that the UN says displaced more than 3,000 people in the city.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the operation after Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers at a Hebron checkpoint on October 23. Both assailants were killed in the attack.

item.title: Isaac Herzog: the mild-mannered middleman in Israel's political brawl
item.description:
By Lili Bayer and Maayan Lubell

JERUSALEM, Nov 2 (Reuters) - In a country where politics has become a bare-knuckled brawl, Isaac Herzog, the mild-mannered president now tasked with persuading Israel's party leaders to lower their fists and form a government, is a throwback to a gentler era.

Though no one would call him naive — he has served both as leader of the opposition against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and as a member of a unity cabinet under him — Herzog's soft-spoken manner can appear out of step with the times.

item.title: Oman’s sultan concludes historic China visit amid US tensions: What to know
item.description: The visit, the first by an Omani head of state since 1978, comes as Oman is reportedly considering purchasing Chinese- and Pakistani-made JF-17 fighter jets as part of efforts to diversify its international partnerships amid growing regional tensions.

item.title: Analysis-Trump's Iran threat renews Gulf fears of a war it didn't choose
item.description:
By Samia Nakhoul, Alexander Cornwell and Timour Azhari

MANAMA, Nov 2 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump’s threat to strike Iran again confronts America’s Gulf allies with a stark prospect: another war decided in Washington in which the US bases built to protect them could instead make them targets for harsh Iranian reprisal.

item.title: Israel army withdraws after Hebron operation
item.description:
Israeli troops withdrew on Monday from an area of the occupied West Bank's largest city that they had evacuated of its Palestinian residents, following an attack that killed two soldiers in October.

The operation had emptied a neighbourhood in Hebron city where the two gunmen had lived, with soldiers later destroying their homes -- a practice commonly carried out by the military as punishment for attacks.

item.title: As peacekeepers leave Western Sahara, refugees yearn to end a half-century wait
item.description:
TINDOUF, Algeria, Nov 2 (Reuters) - At 51, Binina Mohamed is as old as the conflict that drove her from the Western Sahara region into a refugee camp in southern Algeria, where she has spent her life among tens of thousands of others facing a similar fate.

The confrontation over her native land, often described as Africa's longest-running territorial dispute, was brought back into focus this weekend by a UN Security Council spat that led to the end of a decades-old peacekeeping mission there.

item.title: Europe space chief heads to Gulf as bloc looks beyond US
item.description:
By Florence Loeve

PARIS, Nov 2 (Reuters) - The head of the European Space Agency will meet officials in the United Arab Emiratesthis week as Europe seeks new partners and aims to reduce its reliance on the United States for space exploration.

The rise of Elon Musk's SpaceX has laid bare Europe's reliance on American space technology.
